title: Heterogeneous quant noise joinery: latency vs. fidelity matrix
body:
Status: early draft, collection of field notes and experiment fragments.

Goal
- Understand how mixed quant strategies (INT8, FP8, GPTQ, AWQ) interact with heterogeneous kernels across real traffic shapes. We want a compact matrix that maps kernel X quant config -> (p50, p95 latency, token/sec, quality delta) for a handful of representative workloads.

Motivation / motivating questions
- Some kernels give great throughput but introduce intermittent "noise-floor" quality regressions for certain prompt shapes. Is this noise deterministic (per-layer) or stochastic under load?
- How does FP8 behave versus AWQ/GPTQ on long-context bursts (>= 8k tokens) using our KV-cache path?
- Can we identify small changes to kernel selection or scheduling that keep latency SLOs while avoiding worst-case quality hits?

Summary of quick findings (top-level)
- AWQ variant with kernel A2 yields best p50 and throughput for chat-like short prompts, but shows a measurable BLEU/ROUGE drop on code-generation prompts vs FP8 and GPTQ on the same model.
- INT8 with kernel C3 has lower p95 under mixed-small-batches, but exhibits higher variance (jitter) when sequence-length distribution includes many 1-token prompts interleaved with long requests.
- FP8 gives the most consistent quality across datasets but costs ~8-12% more latency on rtx-8000 class hardware with our current kernel implementation.

Experimental setup (notes)
- Models: Llama-2-13B v1.0 (baseline float), Mistral-7B-v0.9 (for smaller model comparisons).
- Quant methods: symmetric per-channel INT8 (our q8a pipeline), AWQ per-tensor asymmetric variant, GPTQ (2-step rounding), FP8 (e4m3-compatible).
- Kernels: kernel-A2 (vectorized fused attention, compiled via custom-cu kernel), kernel-B1 (CuBLAS+hand-tiling), kernel-C3 (experimental lane-branch scheduling).
- Hardware: nVidia A100 40GB (hosted bench instance), rtx-8000 dev nodes (on-prem cluster), inference nodes with mixed PCIe gen3/4.
- Workloads: short-chat (avg len 40 tokens), long-context (avg len 2500 tokens), mixed-burst (heavy 1-token p99 with occasional 4k bursts).
- Client emulation: local client harness, 30k requests replayed from production sampling (redacted). Use arrival trace with peak 1200 qps for throughput runs.

Metrics captured
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 for generation step (first-token + streaming tail), cold-start appended separately.
- Throughput: tokens/sec sustained.
- Resource: GPU util, memory footprint, PCIe transfers, kernel occupancy.
- Quality: perplexity against dev set, pass@k for code tasks, BLEU/ROUGE for summarization, and a small crowd-sourced human eval sample (12 prompts) for catastrophic artifacts (hallucinations, token corruption).
- Determinism: output hash fingerprint stability across 100 repeated runs with identical seeds.

Key experiment logs (fragments)
- 2025-09-18 09:12 — AWQ + kernel-A2 on 13B, short-chat: p50 42ms, p95 110ms, tokens/sec 1450. Perplexity delta vs float: +0.8%. Human eval: trivial.
- 2025-09-18 12:27 — AWQ + kernel-A2 on code-gen set: BLEU down 4.6 points vs float; failing cases show truncated identifier names and occasional token-level corruption around punctuation. Replayed with GPTQ -> BLEU down 1.2 points. FP8 -> BLEU down 0.7 points.
- 2025-09-19 14:03 — INT8 + kernel-C3 mixed-burst: p50 35ms, p95 420ms (big tail), p99 1.7s. Jitter correlates with concurrent short requests triggering small-kernel preemption.
- 2025-09-21 16:18 — FP8 + kernel-B1 on long-context: stable p95 ~780ms, tokens/sec 680, small quality delta vs float. Observed 5% increased VRAM pressure causing slower KV swapping.

Observations / hypotheses
- Kernel micro-tiling decisions interact badly with AWQ's per-row scale metadata; when a kernel does dynamic lane branching it may reorder memory accesses and amplify quantization noise for vector-sensitive layers (e.g., first feedforward layer after attention).
- Jitter in kernel-C3 appears tied to our scheduler's heuristic for merging 1-token requests into existing batches. When merging is disabled, jitter drops but throughput suffers.
- FP8's extra exponent range helps with pathological tokens in code-gen where very small values (weights x activations) cross underflow thresholds in other quant forms. This matches the observed lower token corruption rate.

Quick reproducible recipe (how to run locally)
- Checkout: git checkout feature/hetero-quant-bench
- Start harness: ./bench/harness --model llama-13b --quant awq --kernel a2 --trace traces/mix-202509.json --qps 800 --duration 300
- Capture logs: /tmp/bench-YYYYMMDD.tar.gz (contains perf counters, kernel traces, output samples)
- Re-run with --seed 42 to check determinism.

Failure cases / example artifacts (copy/paste)
- Prompt: "def compute_hash(x):"
  Output snippet (AWQ+A2): "def compute_hsh(x):\n    return x%#"
  Observed: token truncation around symbol sequences.

Next actions (short-term)
- Run targeted layer attribution tests: re-quantize only FFN1/FFN2/AttnProj separately and replay code-gen set to see if corruption localizes. (Owner: Liam)
- Instrument kernel-A2 to log per-layer memory access pattern for AWQ runs. (Owner: Meera)
- Try a scheduler tweak: disallow merge of 1-token requests with existing batches for kernel-C3 and measure throughput tradeoff (Owner: Diego).
- Prepare a 1-page summary for infra + product to decide whether FP8 is worth the latency tax for code-heavy customers (deadline 2025-09-30).

Open questions / risks
- Does the AWQ artifact imply a correctness bug in our quant metadata handling, or is it inherent to AWQ rounding choices?
- What is the long-term cost of preferring FP8 for a subset of customers (hardware utilization impact, license constraints)?
- Are there quick kernel-level fixes (reorder loads / use prefetch) that avoid the amplification without falling back to FP8?

Notes to self / messy checklist (informal)
- collect 50 more code-gen samples that trigger failure (currently only ~8 reproducible).
- ask SRE to run jittered-burst on prod shadows for broader coverage.
- link to old A/B kernel migration doc for scheduler heuristics.

References / links
- perf counters: /mnt/bench/2025-09-18/perf-counters.log
- slack thread: #serving-runtime quant-jitter (see thread pinned message)
- GH PR with AWQ fixes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/695

If this looks useful I'll tidy into a concise matrix CSV and a short slide for ops. For now this is a live working doc: expect gaps, TODOs, and rough command snippets.

-- Aisha
